summary: HATP TRUST-ENROLLMENT / SIGNING HMIC TRANSITIVE AUTHORITY SCOPE INDEPENDENTLY DERIVED -- ALIGNMENT PREREQUISITE DEFINED. Analysis only; zero production source or contract file modified. Read HMIC-001 v1.4's primary contract text (docs/contracts/HATP_MANDATORY_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION_CERTIFICATION_CONTRACT.md, 5103 lines) and its production implementation (hatp_mandatory_certification.py) directly and re-derived HMIC-REQ-052 from first principles rather than reusing any prior phase's summary. HMIC-REQ-052 currently defines exactly three closure limbs (mandatory activation-readiness call graph; the certification module's own self-binding call graph; the Class-B verifier/DeploymentBinding-producer call graph), and none reaches hatp_signing_ceremony.py, hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, or hatp_principal_signer_admin.py -- confirmed directly: hatp_mandatory_cutover.py only checks hatp_signing_ceremony's importability, never calls into it. A fresh Python-ast import-graph walk of all three candidate files, executed in this phase, found every other PCAE-owned dependency already HMIC-bound except four leaf utility/telemetry modules (paths.py, provenance.py, git_status.py, tasks.py), each excluded on the same established repository precedent already applied elsewhere (already transitively imported by a currently-bound file, never separately bound) and confirmed at the call-graph (not blind whole-module) level that the specific symbols used never reach those modules' own broader unrelated fan-out. Exact required implementation/content source-set delta: +3 files (hatp_signing_ceremony.py, hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py, hatp_principal_signer_admin.py; 30 to 33 entries, zero removals). Exact required contract-version-set delta: +2 (HPSE-001 v1.1, HHCE-001 v1.1, currently unbound for both content and version; 5 to 7 members), mirroring the HBDC-001 v1.2 content+version-binding precedent rather than a version-only binding. Independently confirmed HSCE-001 v1.3 is already fully and correctly represented in current HMIC identity for both content (frozen-file member #26) and version (dynamically re-read from the live contract header, never hardcoded) -- no gap there. BF-1, BF-2, B-149O.20L.7O.2F.3-1, and B-149O.20L.7O.2F.3-2 all independently reconfirmed still closed at their respective implementation boundaries, unchanged since 2F.5 (zero commits touched the relevant files). Class-B verifier files (topology/environment-lock/conformance) remain bound and unchanged since well before 2F; CBV-S1 unaffected (Class-B's own closure is already complete, the gap identified in this phase concerns a separate authority surface); CBV-S10 remains OPEN, untouched, no readiness Boolean invented. Selected recommendation among Options A/B/C/D: Option A -- one additive HMIC-001 contract-evolution phase adding a new closure limb (d) to HMIC-REQ-052 (mirroring the existing limb (b)/(c) self-binding/dual-anchor construction), widening HMIC-REQ-050 to the derived 33-file set and the contract-version set to the derived 7-member set, with production constants realigned in the same phase as the contract amendment per the 149O.20L.7K precedent (not the split 149O.20K sequencing). No HMIC modification, repin, certification, activation, or provisioning occurred in this phase. A new 11-test independent analysis suite (mechanical re-validation of the current 30/5 baseline extraction, the fresh import-graph closure, target-set determinism/existence, HPSE-001/HHCE-001 header parsing, HSCE-001 v1.3 binding, and Class-B-unchanged status) passed 11/11. Fast Green exact node-ID diff against an isolated disposable worktree at the phase-entry commit found one current-only failure (tests/test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_audit_verify_cli, an unrelated pcae shell-gate audit verify CLI subprocess test with a 15-second timeout), independently re-run in isolation without concurrent -n auto worker contention and confirmed to pass in 13.38 seconds -- system-load-induced timing flakiness from running two full parallel fast_green invocations concurrently during the comparison, not a regression: this phase touched zero files related to shell-gate/audit, so the durable regression count attributable to this phase's changes is 0 failed.
